summary: Santa Barbara County cabin on McKinley Mountain, built 1935, later an Aircraft Warning Service station; Forest Service removed it in 1974 after high winds.

facts.design: cabin in a sandstone-encircled clearing east of the official peak
facts.status_note: Forest Service removed the cabin in 1974 after high winds destroyed it; a 2013 account says some remains are at the top

access.note: On foot up a steep half-mile use trail from McKinley Saddle, in the San Rafael Wilderness

visit.trail_note: The road effectively ends at McKinley Saddle, at the western Mission Pine trailhead; a steep half-mile use trail climbs west to the top

events.note: Cabin built in 1935, per records cited by a 2011 blog and a 2013 trail account
Forest Service removed the cabin after high winds had destroyed it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Songs of the Wilderness says Aircraft Warning System; Craig Carey and Wikipedia say Aircraft Warning Service. The story uses Aircraft Warning Service.

notes_for_editor: Two independent personal accounts (sources 2 and 3) agree on the 1935 build and the 1974 removal after high winds. Neither gives a date for the Aircraft Warning Service use. No government or NHLR record was in cache. The access level public rests on the trail description, not on a Forest Service statement. The brief had kind unknown; the FFLOS list types it AWS. No photos were added.
